description: Financial and lending specific risk scoring rules for loan and amendment analysis.

entries.text: HIGH risk: Broad release of claims language that waives known and unknown claims against lender can materially limit remediation options.

metadata.suggested_fix: Narrow release scope to known claims as of execution date and preserve fraud/gross-negligence carve-outs.

entries.text: HIGH risk: Conditions subsequent with immediate default trigger may create accelerated default exposure without cure period.

metadata.suggested_fix: Add notice and cure windows; make default trigger proportional to materiality.

entries.text: MEDIUM risk: Amendment fee calculated on total commitment instead of incremental increase can materially overcharge borrower.

metadata.suggested_fix: Tie fee basis to incremental commitment increase or negotiated cap.

entries.text: MEDIUM risk: Mandatory quarterly principal or commitment reductions can stress liquidity and increase refinancing pressure.

metadata.suggested_fix: Negotiate reduction schedule flexibility or performance-based step-down triggers.

entries.text: MEDIUM risk: Sole discretion language in lender rights can create one-sided enforcement and interpretation outcomes.

metadata.suggested_fix: Add objective standards, reasonableness qualifiers, and notice obligations.

entries.text: LOW to MEDIUM risk: Jury trial waivers are common in commercial lending but should be highlighted for litigation strategy impact.

metadata.suggested_fix: Confirm jurisdictional enforceability and evaluate strategic litigation trade-offs.

entries.text: MEDIUM risk: Submission to distant or out-of-state jurisdiction may increase defense costs and procedural burden.

metadata.suggested_fix: Negotiate neutral or home-state venue, or add arbitration venue compromise.
